sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and names two example enablers
sections.what: Imports the test tools, the enabler identifier type and the deduplicate function, and gives two enablers short names, DOC and TRIAGE, for use in the tests.
sections.why: Likely reason: short names let the tests refer to two real capabilities without repeating their full identifiers.
sections.watch_out: The tests depend on these two enablers existing in the schema enumeration.

sections.name: TestTheRatioSaysWhatItMeans
sections.title: Checks what the duplication ratio means
sections.what: Runs small made-up portfolios through the deduplication step and checks the results. Independent processes should show no duplication. Several processes claiming one shared capability should count as one capability. The shared pool should equal the largest claim, not the sum of claims.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the basic rules the rest of the value calculation depends on, so they are checked first on simple inputs.
sections.watch_out: The ratio is only meaningful if the even split rule for a lone process with two capabilities is kept. Removing it lets the ratio fall below one.

sections.name: TestNobodyIsCreditedMoreThanTheyClaimed
sections.title: Checks no process gets more than it claimed
sections.what: Checks that credited effort never exceeds a process's own claim, including unusual cases such as a tiny claim with a huge baseline or a zero baseline. It also checks that any capped excess still shows up in the total instead of disappearing.
sections.why: The class notes say an earlier rule credited a small claimant many times what it ever said it would save, which made the portfolio total wrong.
sections.watch_out: These caps are the main guard against inflated figures. If someone loosens them, these tests should turn red.

sections.name: TestABandEndMayLegitimatelyBeZero
sections.title: Checks zero low cases are allowed
sections.what: Confirms that a portfolio whose values are all zero still builds, and that only the duplication ratio refuses to be calculated in that case, with a message calling it a downside case. It also confirms that an empty portfolio is refused with a clear message.
sections.why: The class notes say raising an error when the object is built made the whole engine fail on a legitimate low case.
sections.watch_out: Do not turn zero values into build-time errors. The ratio is the only place that should refuse.

sections.name: TestThePoolModelRefusesASummedPool
sections.title: Checks the pool model rejects summed pools
sections.what: Checks that the EnablerPool model accepts a pool equal to the largest single claim. It rejects a pool equal to the sum of claims, and rejects any pool above the largest claim, with messages about double counting.
sections.why: The class notes say an earlier check compared two fields that were set from the same calculation, so it could never fail. This test checks the model's own refusal.
sections.watch_out: This validator is the only guard against double counting. Disabling it must make these tests fail.

summary: Sets up tests for the deduplication step, which counts a shared capability once and reports how much double counting was avoided.
purpose: Checks that shared enablers, meaning capabilities used by several processes, are counted once, and that the duplication ratio reports this correctly.
why: The docstring says the double count is the failure this package exists to prevent, and the ratio is the figure a finance team asks about first.
how: Only the setup section was supplied for this review, so the test steps are not explained here.
inputs: Enabler ids from the schema enumeration, and the deduplicate function.
outputs: Pass or fail for each test.
risks: From the setup section alone, the risks cannot be judged. The tests depend on two specific enabler ids existing in the schema.
debug: Start with the deduplicate function in packages/value/dedupe.py, then check the enabler ids used in the tests exist in the schema enumeration.
